OK, so Godot is actually fixing this for you. What it doesn't do is save the changes to disk. The new UID assigned to the resources with a duplicate UID are stored in memory and don't flush out to disk until you save the scenes.

For the most part this is part of a safety mechanism that when opening a project in a newer version of Godot, it doesn't start saving out a whole bunch of small unnecesairy changes. But I'd argue that in this case, we should trigger an automatic save of the resource/scene when a duplicate UID is found.

That said, there is a related issue here. What isn't an unlikely scenario is that it's not just a single file you're duplicating, often you're duplicating a folder.
Say you have a folder with an NPC setup, and you duplicate that folder to start working on a new NPC variant, that duplicate NPC now has duplicate UIDs with the old NPC. They get new UIDs on load BUT if that setup consists of multiple files, internal references may cause parts of the new NPC variant to reference files within the original NPC variant.

Originally I was thinking this could be fixed by preferencing the path over the UID but now that I think of it, that wouldn't work in this situation either because even the path is wrong. The only thing that would work here is if we allow relative paths instead of absolute paths in our scene files.

> OK, so Godot is actually fixing this for you. What it doesn't do is save the changes to disk. The new UID assigned to the resources with a duplicate UID are stored in memory and don't flush out to disk until you save the scenes.

Interesting! I did not realize this.

> For the most part this is part of a safety mechanism that when opening a project in a newer version of Godot, it doesn't start saving out a whole bunch of small unnecesairy changes. But I'd argue that in this case, we should trigger an automatic save of the resource/scene when a duplicate UID is found.

If it's as easy as you say, then I feel like we should definitely tack this onto the new "Upgrade UIDs..." action that's been added to the "Project > Tools" menu in that case, which I believe is what runs when you first upgrade a project to 4.4.

> BUT if that setup consists of multiple files, internal references may cause parts of the new NPC variant to reference files within the original NPC variant.

It's certainly a related issue, but I would probably say that this should be considered out of scope for this particular issue, since it's not necessarily a new thing in 4.4, and something you would get tripped up on in 4.3 as well (if I understand you correctly).

I guess my focus is more on the stuff that generally worked (however questionable) in 4.3 and is now considered grounds for emitting warnings every time you launch the editor, with no real recourse other than to mess with the contents of the resource files yourself, manually or otherwise.

> OK, so Godot is actually fixing this for you. What it doesn't do is save the changes to disk. The new UID assigned to the resources with a duplicate UID are stored in memory and don't flush out to disk until you save the scenes.

To follow up on this, opening the scenes and immediately saving them seems to resolve the issue.
However, this is not the case for resources, as there is no way to simply "save" them presumably without re-importing.

In my project, the duplicate UIDs were for two different scenes (and indeed one was originally a copy of the other). However I could not find a way to get Godot to fix the problem for me. I tried:

1. Just saving the project after seeing the warnings
2. Opening the 2 affected scenes simultaneously; saving both
3. Assigning the two scenes to a property of a third scene & saving all 3 scenes (there weren't any direct references to the affected scenes in other scenes)

None of these had any effect.

In the end I created a new scene, copied its UID, deleted it, and then manually edited one of the `.tscn` files to use the new UID.

As I am nowhere near understanding where the issues I am having actually lie and I am not getting any error messages that are plausible (Error: script missing while script is not missing), this is a frustrating experience and is blocking progress on 3 of my projects.

@BastiaanOlij wrote:
> OK, so Godot is actually fixing this for you. What it doesn't do is save the changes to disk.

Bbehavior like this - changing UUIDs on the fly without actually changing them - seems like exactly like something that would lead to [unexpected load errors when for instance two scenes actually share a class](#105021) for instance.

Users _need to be able to resolve UUID collisions_ when they happen so they can get back to a stable and reproducible state.

Just stumbled upon this issue in 4.4.1.stable after duplicating a scene, then swapping both scenes' names.

> WARNING: editor/editor_file_system.cpp:1358 - UID duplicate detected between res://level_4.tscn and res://level_3.tscn.

I duplicated scene level_3.tscn with the name level_4.tscn. Then, by accident, I edited level_3.tscn instead of level_4.tscn, so I decided to just rename them. At this point I was unable to input level_3.tscn anywhere using the Inspector, because Godot was automatically replacing it with level_4.tscn, accompanied by the warning. Deleting level_4.tscn seems to have fixed everything.

Duplicating level_3.tscn again does not result in either the issue or any warnings, so I'm guessing the renaming played a role here.

> I'm not sure what the fix should be, especially considering that you don't really have a reliable notion of a newer versus older file in these kinds of cases, like you do when new files are added ([#100927](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100927)) while the editor is running. 

I think we can use the uid cache file (`.godot/uid_cache.bin`) to detect new and old files.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9b50ea8adec073c891763f7c8c2844bf207cf103/editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp#L506

`unique_ids` in `ResourceUID` should be maintained before and after scans in `EditorFileSystem`: Verify that the uid is valid and then purge only invalid uid entries. 


Note that there are two types of scans in `EditorFileSystem`:
1. `EditorFileSystem::scan()`, used to **(re)build** the file system tree. 
2. `EditorFileSystem::scan_changes()`, used to **update** the file system tree.

Returning to the editor from outside while the editor is running triggers `EditorFileSystem::scan_changes()`.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9b50ea8adec073c891763f7c8c2844bf207cf103/editor/editor_node.cpp#L934

 However, when processing externally added (renamed) directories, its processing logic is similar to `EditorFileSystem::scan()`, calling `EditorFileSystem::_process_file_system()`, that seems to be designed only for building directory file trees..

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9b50ea8adec073c891763f7c8c2844bf207cf103/editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp#L1471

In this case, if a copy of the directory is created, you will not receive any warning until you restart the editor. No new uid is generated.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9b50ea8adec073c891763f7c8c2844bf207cf103/editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp#L1371-L1380

What’s worse is that it replaces the uid, and appends the record to the end of `.godot/uid_cache.bin` by calling `ResourceUID::update_cache()`.


https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9b50ea8adec073c891763f7c8c2844bf207cf103/core/io/resource_uid.cpp#L272-L284

According to the logic of `ResourceUID::load_from_cache()`, the latest record will overwrite the previous one. So after restarting the editor, you may lose the opportunity to determine which file is older.

While this ticket is mostly for `.tres` and `.tscn` files, at least three now have had issues with `.res` files getting the same error message.

I have [a script](https://github.com/TokisanGames/Terrain3D/blob/dae01b178f7d3fc681d682b57b56871285d25c3c/project/addons/terrain_3d/tools/region_mover.gd) that renames res files using DirAccess::rename(). It moves a whole Terrain3D world by renaming the region files in sequence to avoid name collisions. I.e. It renames files like `terrain3d_05_05.res` to `tmp_terrain3d_00_00.res` to `terrain3d_00_00.res`.

After doing so and restarting the editor, my editor reports many res files with duplicate UIDs.

```
WARNING: UID duplicate detected between res://scenes/terrains/world/terrain3d_04-06.res and res://scenes/terrains/world/terrain3d_03-07.res.
     at: _process_file_system (editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp:1377)
```

**What doesn't work:**
* Opening the editor, saving and restarting
* Opening the res files in the inspector and resaving them. This changes the file, detected by git, but doesn't change the UID.

**What did work:**
1. In the editor, renaming one of the files by adding a 'b' before the '.res', and then renaming it back where the error is `UID duplicate between A and B`. 

    Usually renaming A didn't work and I had to rename B. Occasionally I had to rename A. For many files, I'd rename one file and then it would conflict with a different one, and I got to the point where I was renaming files but they just picked new files to conflict with and I couldn't fix the whole list.

    I don't think this step is necessary, nor reliable.

2. Outside of Godot I moved all my problem res files to another folder, came back to godot, saved, restarted. Outside of Godot moved the res files back, switched to godot. It imported them all and reported many errors `Unrecognized UID: xxxxxx`. Saved, restarted.  No more errors. 

    Git reports these as modified files.

3. I closed Godot, then reverted all of my res files in git. Then I reopened Godot. No more errors.

So in conclusion
* My res files are exactly the same.
* Any conflicting UID is not in my files. The UID conflict is only in Godot's files.
* I used the API to rename the file, so this is 100% caused by Godot.
* Perhaps I can work around it by forcing a new UID with Resource.set_uid()#87714.

(tested in v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439])

After getting a conflict between 2 scenes with same guid (due to a Git merge between two versions that originated from a very old common commit), I got the "Duplicate UID" warning (at first it didn't show, I had to restart the editor). In fact, hovering over the two scenes, I could see that they already got different uids (not the case before editor restart), but it wasn't saved on disk as mentioned in the 2nd comment.

Anyway, I deleted one of the scenes. Yet, when dragging the remaining scene to some `@export_file("*.tscn") var target_level_path: String = ""` property in the inspector, it would keep showing the deleted scene name (even though their uid were supposed to be different at this point!)

Even weirder, I restarted the editor and this time the reference was properly pointing to the remaining scene, which had reverted to its original uid (it really wasn't saved on disk even after manual save!)

I didn't try reimporting the files, I saw the comment about that afterward, maybe it could have helped. Anyway, all of this is probably just symptoms from the wrong cache/update logic you found in the code. Just another use case to check once this is fixed.

> for a manual Fix what should someone do?

@MisamotoGames what worked for me when encountering duplicate UID on scene (`.tscn`) files:
1. Close the editor
2. Delete the `.godot/` directory (probably just deleting `.godot/uid_cache.bin` is sufficient, but not sure)
3. Open affected `.tscn` files in an external editor and remove the `uid="uid://$VALUE"` attribute from the `gd_scene` definition at the top.
4. Open the editor, load the scenes and save them

I've had an issue involving duplicate UIDs for a month now where the wrong scene was loaded, leading me to think the engine had spontaneously deleted things.  If the engine can detect duplicates it would be nice to have a warning about it so it's immediately known.
